title: Demolition: remove convention promotion/lifecycle/proposal machinery
description:
Per the sutra/176 decision (arc sutra/~12): delete the promotion/lifecycle half of the convention system.

Remove:
- `src/conventions/lifecycle.rs` (detect_signals, generate_proposals) and its call sites in the review pipeline (`build_findings`)
- Tables + Db methods: `convention_proposals`, `convention_state`, `convention_history` (convention_state and convention_proposals are Durable — need explicit DROP migrations; history is Ephemeral)
- MCP actions on `sutra_conventions`: promote, demote, proposals, and any lifecycle-state surfacing in list output
- `record_convention_history` and proposal generation in `src/tools/review.rs` build_findings

Notes:
- There are ~6 human-set convention_state rows across workspaces (arrow, backend, explore, sutra). Before dropping, check each: if any encodes a rule worth keeping, translate it to a hand-written constraint rule (rules TOML) — that is the designated enforcement path now. The known one (kind:const → naming:SCREAMING) duplicates a rustc lint; likely none survive.
- The pending-proposal queues across all workspace DBs (~1,200 rows) disappear with the table drop — no separate dismiss_all needed.
- Update `docs/conventions-map.md` (lifecycle section, data-flow diagram, table list) as part of this task.
- Mind the refactor contract discipline in CLAUDE.md: review output field semantics must not silently shift — removing proposals/lifecycle from output is intentional; document it in the map.

Acceptance: cargo test passes; reindex of a workspace writes no proposal/state/history rows; sutra_conventions tool surface reduced accordingly; conventions-map.md updated.
execution_record: Straightforward demolition. Checked 6 convention_state rows across 4 workspace DBs (arrow, backend, explore, sutra) — all naming conventions already enforced by language linters, none needed translation to constraint rules. Simplified delete_stale_conventions to remove convention_state subquery (no more protection for stateful conventions since state is gone). Changed orient output from lifecycle-categorized sections (preferred/deprecated/forbidden/descriptive) to a single observed_patterns section. Removed convention_matches from review output (was only populated for deprecated/forbidden conventions). Pre-existing test_field_access_skipped failure in resolver_test.rs is unrelated.

Codex adversarial review (covers sutra/231 + sutra/232 together, diff 6ce098e..af9c6f0):

Verdict: needs-attention (3 findings)

1. [high] Reindex resurrects dropped tables — ephemeral CREATE migrations (0016, 0020, 0022, 0034, 0036) rerun after reindex wipes their schema_migrations entries, but durable DROP migrations (0044, 0045) are skipped. Tables get recreated.
2. [high] cargo test gate not met — test_field_access_skipped in resolver_test.rs fails deterministically, but is pre-existing (not caused by this diff).
3. [medium] Stale MCP help text — src/tools/help.rs:319-320 still advertises "signature templates, anti-pattern warnings, drift alerts, waivers, and pending proposals" for orient, which were removed.

Finding 1 is the only ship-blocking issue from the demolition itself.
